deep.reconstruction:
Context: this folio continues the preceding pages. Those pages list the primes 401-997 crossed off as done, plus the prime powers 4, 8, 16; 9, 27, 81, 243, 729; 7, 49, 343; 11, 121. The work is Gauss's table of decimal periods of fractions a/p, the material behind Disquisitiones Arithmeticae arts. 312-318 and the posthumous 'Tafel zur Verwandlung gemeiner Brüche in Decimalbrüche' (Werke II). For each modulus m he writes one full period of a/m for one numerator a from each coset of the subgroup <10> in (Z/m)*. Writing starts at the first nonzero digit; a dot marks where the period restarts, and the first repeated digits are underlined.

(1) m = 193. ord_193(10) = 192 = phi(193), so one period suffices. 1/193 = 0.\overline{0051813471 50259...}. Gauss writes 200 digits beginning '5181347150 ...' and ending '...0103626943 00|51813471'. The repeat begins at the dotted 5.
[Mine] The structure shows how the expansion was generated. 10^10 ≡ 97 ≡ 1/2 (mod 193). So each 10-digit block is half the previous one, carrying 10^10 when the previous block is odd: B_{k+1} = floor((r_k*10^10 + B_k)/2), where r_k = B_k mod 2. For example 5181347150 -> 2590673575 -> 1295336787 -> 5647668393 -> 7823834196 -> 8911917098 -> ... -> 0103626943 -> 0051813471. Every block on the page satisfies this.

(2) m = 197. ord_197(10) = 98 = phi/2, so two cosets are needed.
- 1/197: period 98, beginning 00507614213... Written: 5076142131 9796954314 7208121827 4111675126 / 9035532994 9238578680 2030456852 7918781725 / 888324873 0964467005 |07. The third row has a 9-digit block, but the digit string is correct; '07' marks the repeat.
- 2/197 (the other coset): 1015228426 3959390862 9441624365 4822335025 3 / 8071065989 8477157360 4060913705 5837563451 / 7766497461 9289340|101. The repeat is underlined '101'.

(3) m = 169 = 13^2. ord(10) = 78 and phi = 156, so two cosets.
- 1/169 = 0.\overline{005917159763...8520710}: 80 digits written, the repeat '59' underlined.
- 2/169 = 0.\overline{01183431952...97041420}: repeat '11' underlined.

(4) m = 121 = 11^2. ord(10) = 22 and phi = 110, so five cosets.
- Gauss writes the periods of 1/121, 2/121, 3/121, 4/121 and 5/121, each 22 digits, with the restart digits '82', '16', '24', '33', '41'.
- [Mine] Why these numerators suffice: <10> reduces mod 11 to {±1}. The cosets of <10> therefore correspond bijectively to (Z/11)*/{±1}, whose representatives are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.
- So the list is complete, hence 'Explicitus' (done). The marginal 100, 20, 30, 40, 50 and the coloured/bracketed marks are bookkeeping, probably checks of numerators and coset membership.

(5) m = 211. 1/211 = 0.\overline{004739336492890995260663507109}, period 30. Written: 4739336492 8909952606 6350710900 4739.... Only this coset is written here; phi/30 = 7 cosets exist.

(6) m = 223. ord(10) = 222 = phi. 1/223 is written in full: 220 digits from '4484304932' to '...2466367713', then '00' completing the period, then '448' (underlined) as the repeat.

At the foot, a faint scribble '1175355440' and '23' is not interpretable with confidence.
errors: 197, first period: the third row groups '888324873' as 9 digits (then '0964467005 07'). The digit stream 8883248730964467005|07 is correct; only the blocking is irregular.

2/197: the true digits after 9441624365 are 4822335025 3, i.e. an 11-digit chunk so that the next row can begin at 8071065989 (which Gauss does). The written group, with its interlinear insertion, as transcribed '4822350253', still lacks one '3'. Gauss evidently noticed an omission and corrected it; whether the correction is complete cannot be settled from the transcription. All subsequent digits are correct.
197, second period, last row: one digit in '7766497461' is overwritten. The final reading 7766497461 is correct.
No arithmetic errors found in the periods of 1/193, 1/169, 2/169, a/121 (a = 1..5), 1/211, 1/223 as checked.

results.what: Full decimal periods of a/p for p = 193, 197, 169, 121, 211, 223, with one period per coset of <10> in (Z/m)*
results.modern_name: Decimal (repetend) tables; multiplicative order of 10 mod m; coset decomposition of (Z/m)* by <10>
results.usually_credited_to: Tables of reciprocals/periods: J.H. Lambert, J. Bernoulli III, Robertson, Henry Goodwyn (c.1760s-1820s); theory of the period length: Euler, Lambert, Gauss (DA 1801)

results.what: Generating the 1/193 period block-wise by repeated halving, using 10^10 ≡ 1/2 (mod 193)
results.modern_name: Computing repetends via a power of the base congruent to a simple fraction (multiplication/division by small factor per block)
results.usually_credited_to: Standard computational device; Gauss describes related shortcuts for computing periods in DA art. 315-317

results.what: Completeness check for 121: numerators 1..5 represent all cosets of <10> mod 121 ('Explicitus')
results.modern_name: Index/coset structure of the subgroup generated by 10 in (Z/p^2)*

deep.surprise_reason: This is working material for Gauss's well-known table of decimal periods for denominators under 1000, described in Disquisitiones arts. 312-318 and printed from the Nachlass in Werke II. The halving shortcut for 193 is a routine computational device.

checkable.asserts: 10 is a primitive root mod 193, so one period covers all fractions a/193
10^10 ≡ 1/2 mod 193, explaining the halving of successive 10-digit blocks
start of the 2/197 period, showing the correct digits 4822335025
period length 78 for 1/169, hence two cosets

transcription_corrections: 197, second (unlabelled) period, row 1, 4th group: correct digits are 4822335025 followed by 3 (11 digits before 8071065989). The transcription '48{+2+}2350253' records an interlinear correction but the resulting string lacks a '3'.
197, first period, row 3: '888324873 0964467005 07' is Gauss's blocking; the stream reads 8883248730 9644670050 7.
The unlabelled block after 197 is the period of 2/197 (second coset), and the rows 3-4 under 169 are the period of 2/169.
121 block: the rows are the periods of 1/121, 2/121, 3/121, 4/121, 5/121. The marginal '100, 20, 30, 40, 50' and '(2)', '(1)', '22', '44' are bookkeeping marks, not part of the digit strings.
Foot of page: '1175355440' and '23' are faint and uncertain; no matching period was identified.
